info.name: onlinesupport-go-ai / tests
info.description:
Assertion collection: negative cases, timing probes, signature checks, coverage smoke.

For a plain fire-and-read route list, use `onlinesupport-go-ai / api`. Both share one environment.

Every `/v1` response uses the envelope `{"success":bool,"data":...,"error":{"code","message"}}` (internal/transport/http/response/envelope.go), so test scripts read `data.*`. `GET /healthz` is the one exception.

Folder and request names here are asserted by `scripts/swagger/postman_test.go` — rename in both places or the Go test fails.

request.description: The local off-domain guard runs before the router and cache. An off-domain hit should return `status: off_domain` without paying for an LLM call.

request.description: Run this immediately before `chat: KB repeat cache timing`. It seeds the exact-transcript response cache with `chat_cache_probe`.
Byte-identical transcript to the cold request. The cache TTL is `CHAT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 300s), so send this within 5 minutes of the cold call.
Only `user` and `assistant` roles are accepted. Transcripts are truncated to the last 12 messages and 16000 characters.

request.description: An AI-guessed symptom is only anchored when its confidence clears the gate (0.70). `ai_symptom_conf` is accepted as an alias.

exec: pm.test("graph anchor skipped for low confidence", function () {

request.description: Confidence 0.25 is below the gate, so the planner records a skip reason instead of anchoring the graph.
Most useful when the tenant has `kb_chunks` child rows with a `parent_chunk_id`, so parent context can be expanded around a child hit.
`message` is required. `query` is accepted as an alias and is copied into `message` during normalization.
Allowed channels: line, email, web, voice, api, in_app.
Go must receive references to media Laravel already stored, never raw bytes or `data:` URLs.
An attachment needs at least one of `id`, `url` or `storage_key`.
Permission `ai:search:read`. `types` defaults to `["kb"]` and `limit` defaults to 10.
`kb` is currently the only supported search type.
Valid range is 1 to 50.
Run `Reply Draft > reply` first so `ai_action_id` is populated. Scores: accepted 2, edited 1, escalated 0, rejected -1.

request.description: Permission `ai:review:approve`. No request body. Approving promotes the proposed node into the tenant graph.
Permission `ai:review:reject`. The body is optional; a malformed body is ignored rather than rejected.

exec: message: { id: messageId, type: "text", text: pm.environment.get("tenant_known_issue") },
pm.test("conversation and message were persisted", function () {

request.description:
Public route: no JWT and no `X-Tenant-Id`. The tenant is resolved from the receiving channel account. Signature is base64 `HMAC-SHA256(raw_body)` keyed with `LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET`.

Only `events[0]` is read. An `image` event becomes a synthetic `image/jpeg` attachment with an empty body; `audio` becomes `audio/m4a`.
When a channel-specific verifier is registered it runs exclusively. A generic `X-AI-Signature` header will not rescue a LINE request.

exec: subject: "Damaged packaging on my last order",

request.description:
Email has no dedicated verifier, so it falls back to the generic `X-AI-Signature: sha256=<hex>` check keyed with `LARAVEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

Routing is by receiver: `to` must match a `channel_accounts` row, otherwise the response is 404 `not_found` "unknown receiver".
Only `line` and `email` normalizers are registered in `cmd/api`. Bodies over 1 MiB return 413 `payload_too_large`.
No bearer token and no `X-Tenant-Id`. In dev mode (no key material configured) this fails with `missing_tenant`; with JWT verification on it fails with `unauthorized`.

exec: pm.test("status 403 when a service token is configured", function () {
pm.expect.fail("set service_token first, this case only applies with JWT verification on");

request.description: When both are present, `X-Tenant-Id` must equal the token's `cid` claim or the request is forbidden.
Mint `rbac_no_permission_token` with role `customer`, which only carries `ai:feedback:create`. `/v1/reply` needs `ai:reply:create`.
`ai:reports:read` is held by tenant_admin, agent_lead and agent, but not by customer.
Collection naming is `<QDRANT_COLLECTIONPREFIX>__<company_id>`. A green collection with only a couple of points still retrieves badly, so read `points_count`, not just the status.
`candidates: 0` with a healthy Qdrant collection usually means the tenant DB `kb_chunks` table is empty, not that tenancy routing is broken.
